questions.question: Six cases were requested in week 1 and are scheduled to arrive in week 4. None have arrived or been canceled by the end of week 2. How many cases from that request remain outstanding?

options.A: Zero cases, because the request was placed in an earlier week.
options.B: Six cases, because the requested goods have not yet arrived.
options.C: Twelve cases, because two weeks have passed.
options.D: The current physical inventory alone determines the answer.

questions.question: A station has no cases physically available, five unfilled customer cases, and eight earlier requested cases arriving later. Which statement correctly distinguishes these quantities?

options.A: All eight requested cases are physically available now.
options.B: Only the five customer cases are outstanding replenishment.
options.C: The eight later-arriving cases erase the current unfilled customer cases immediately.
options.D: Current stock is zero, five cases are customer obligations, and eight are outstanding replenishment.

questions.question: A shop observes a shortage for two weeks while its first replenishment request is still pending. It submits another request, and both requests later arrive. Which explanation accounts for the two arrivals?

options.A: Both earlier decisions created commitments that could arrive after the shortage was first observed.
options.B: The second request automatically canceled the first one.
options.C: A request becomes a physical receipt as soon as it is submitted.
options.D: Only the most recent shortage can affect later deliveries.

questions.question: Final consumer purchases rise briefly and then return to their previous level. Businesses farther upstream receive changing requests over the following weeks. Which explanation is possible?

options.A: Every upstream request must equal consumer purchases in that same week.
options.B: Changing upstream requests prove that consumer purchases continued rising.
options.C: Businesses' separate responses and delivery delays can propagate a temporary change across later requests.
options.D: Shared inventory information makes all earlier decisions disappear.

display.response_format: JSON object mapping each question_id to one choice letter

deadline_clock.admissible_boundary: complete payload received at or before deadline
deadline_clock.measurement: Local display-open to complete-payload-reception elapsed time, including tool transport, scheduling and output; not verified thinking time or tokens. Expiry is persisted on next access; late admission is always forbidden.
